item.title: [40★] Below-threshold execution of fault-tolerant ripple-carry addition on a trapped-ion quantum computer
item.author: Jacob S. Nelson, Andrew J. Landahl, Andrew D. Baczewski
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 40 ★

Authors: Jacob S. Nelson, Andrew J. Landahl, Andrew D. Baczewski

arXiv ID: 2610.14202 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We deploy a universal fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) architecture based on error-detecting [[8,3,2]][\![8,3,2]\!] and [[4,2,2]][\![4,2,2]\!] codes on Quantinuum's Helios-1 trapped-ion quantum computer. We compile and execute ripple-carry adder (RCA) circuits for classical inputs up to five bits on this architecture. Uncomputing a workspace qubit provides an additional ``algorithmic check'' to detect errors. While available at both the physical and logical levels, this check synergizes with our architecture by increasing the effective fault distance of many circuit locations from two to four. Combining this algorithmic check with the error-detecting codes, we observed only a single logical failure in one-bit addition after burst-error filtering, yielding an estimated logical failure rate of (6.0±5.9)×10−5(6.0 \pm 5.9) \times 10^{-5}. This is well below the (3.5±1.3)×10−3(3.5 \pm 1.3) \times 10^{-3} failure probability observed for one-bit addition on the same hardware in unencoded form. Two- and three-bit adders also showed performance improvements, while the longer four- and five-bit adders executed just above threshold.

Jacob S. Nelson, Andrew J. Landahl, Andrew D. Baczewski

item.title: [35★] The Rényi area law conjecture is false below α=1\alpha=1 in high dimensions
item.author: Tomotaka Kuwahara
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 35 ★

Authors: Tomotaka Kuwahara

arXiv ID: 2610.15199 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Area laws express the expectation that entanglement in gapped quantum ground states scales with a boundary rather than a volume. In one dimension this holds for every Rényi entropy, and the Rényi area-law conjecture asserts the same in higher dimensions for each fixed 0<α<10<\alpha<1. Here we disprove this conjecture in every spatial dimension two and higher. We construct finite-range Hamiltonians with fixed local dimension, bounded interaction strength, unique ground states and a uniform spectral gap, whose ground states exhibit volume-law Rényi entanglement while obeying a von Neumann area law and remaining connected to product states through uniformly gapped local paths. The mechanism is error-space complexity: locally identifiable components of arbitrarily small weight can encode states with high entanglement complexity. We also establish the worst-case rank-error trade-off for approximate ground-state projectors, a key tool in one-dimensional area-law proofs. At fixed gap, the optimal Schmidt rank at projection error ϵ\epsilon across a planar cut of cross-section AA scales as exp[˜Θ((Alogϵ−1)2/3)]\exp[\tilde{\Theta}((A\log\epsilon^{-1})^{2/3})] when logϵ−1≳A\log\epsilon^{-1}\gtrsim A. Thus α=1\alpha=1 is the sharp threshold for a universal Rényi area law within this adiabatically connected class.

Tomotaka Kuwahara

item.title: [22★] TT-efficient unitary synthesis via block-sparse Hamiltonian simulation
item.author: Diyi Liu, ..., David Williams-Young, Chao Yang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 22 ★

Authors: Diyi Liu, ..., David Williams-Young, Chao Yang

arXiv ID: 2610.18589 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We construct Clifford+TT circuits implementing arbitrary nn-qubit unitaries with worst-case TT-count ˜O(N8/7)\widetilde{O}(N^{8/7}) at constant operator-norm error, where N=2nN=2^n, improving the previous exponent 5/45/4. The construction uses ˜O(N6/7)\widetilde{O}(N^{6/7}) clean ancillas. The main idea is to reduce the data addressed by each query to the block-encoding circuit for a sparse piece while controlling the additional simulation work needed to combine the pieces. We simulate a Hermitian logarithm of the target by flattening its traceless part with a two-layer random similarity transformation, randomly partitioning the transformed generator into block-sparse Hermitian pieces, and combining their evolutions using qDRIFT. For a target operator-norm error ϵ∈(0,1/2)\epsilon\in(0,1/2), let L=log2(N/ϵ)L=\log_2(N/\epsilon), the qubit count plus the requested bits of accuracy. By successively correcting the approximation error, we obtain a circuit using ˜O(N8/7L3/7+NL)\widetilde{O}(N^{8/7}L^{3/7}+NL) TT gates and ˜O(N)\widetilde{O}(N) clean ancillas whenever L≤NL\le N. We also prove that, at constant precision, the exponent 8/78/7 is optimal within a sequential block-SELECT model.

Diyi Liu, ..., David Williams-Young, Chao Yang

item.title: [22★] Exponential Quantum Advantage in Stationary Signal Sensing
item.author: Sojeong Park, Changhun Oh
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 22 ★

Authors: Sojeong Park, Changhun Oh

arXiv ID: 2610.14424 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Sensing time-varying signals is essential for precision measurement and for characterizing fluctuations in physical systems. In this work, we show that quantum entanglement provides an exponential advantage in the acquisition time required to learn the temporal statistics of a stationary classical signal. The task is to estimate the characteristic function of joint displacements on selected bosonic modes within a fixed-duration window, using continuous measurements of one signal realization. We present an entanglement-assisted scheme based on two-mode squeezed probes and local Bell measurements with protected idlers, and bound its acquisition time accounting for readout noise and correlations between signal windows. For a strictly stationary pulse family, it achieves polynomial acquisition time at inverse-polynomial accuracy with logarithmic squeezing and polynomial photon number. On the other hand, we prove that any local idler-free protocols require acquisition time exponential in the number of selected temporal modes per window. This lower bound holds for both sequentially prepared and arbitrarily temporally entangled probes, allowing non-Gaussian inputs and measurements and causal classical feedback, as long as each output is measured destructively within its time bin. These results establish an exponential quantum learning advantage for a single continuously monitored stationary signal, with the sensing cost measured by total acquisition time.

Sojeong Park, Changhun Oh

item.title: [17★] Bell's go theorem: regaining local causality with a new notion of realism
item.author: Lorenzo Catani, Nesta van der Schaaf, Rui Soares Barbosa
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 17 ★

Authors: Lorenzo Catani, Nesta van der Schaaf, Rui Soares Barbosa

arXiv ID: 2610.16493 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Bell's theorem is popularly stated as the inconsistency of quantum theory with local realism. Realism is here formalized by the ontological models framework, where elements of reality are points of a measurable space and probabilities obey the Kolmogorov axioms. In the Bell scenario, locally causal ontological models posit a common cause supporting a global valuation, a joint assignment of outcomes to all measurements at once, across incompatible contexts. Within this notion of realism, Bell's theorem makes any realist explanation of the quantum predictions conspiratorial: any mechanism, whether superluminal, superdeterministic, or retrocausal, must be finely tuned so as never to manifest operationally. We redefine realism through a new ontological framework that generalizes the standard one. The elements of reality, which we call records, are no longer points but relational parts of a point-free generalization of a topological space (sublocales of a locale). A record shared by two incompatible contexts establishes the sameness of a measurement across them, without such pairwise identities composing into a global valuation, and the common cause is then a web of such records. Within this framework, Bell's no-go theorem becomes a go theorem: local causality, restated for records, is no longer at odds with the quantum statistics. This is possible because modularity, the inclusion-exclusion law of classical probability, fails across incompatible contexts, so that the probability theory generalizes Kolmogorov's. We exhibit explicit models reproducing several quantum strategies, including the optimal CHSH violation. More broadly, locally causal models of this kind attain every Bell-CHSH value up to the algebraic maximum. A realist explanation of the quantum predictions need not be conspiratorial; every causal influence posited by these models is reflected in the operational predictions.

Lorenzo Catani, Nesta van der Schaaf, Rui Soares Barbosa

item.title: [16★] Quantum simultaneous decoding via pretty-good measurements of tilted states
item.author: Mark M. Wilde
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 16 ★

Authors: Mark M. Wilde

arXiv ID: 2610.15955 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A multiple-access channel transmits messages from several senders to one receiver. For quantum outputs, the receiver must distinguish states depending on all messages, while tests for different decoding errors may not commute. In this paper, we give a self-contained account of simultaneous decoding, in which one joint measurement recovers the messages at the established achievable rates using independent codebooks. The proof combines Sen's tilted-subspace method with Cheng's analysis of the pretty-good measurement, a standard measurement for distinguishing quantum states. Auxiliary labels close to a common reference state separate the geometric directions associated with different errors. A Gram-matrix bound then allows separately chosen binary tests to certify the performance of one measurement. The labels are removed from the completed decoder, leading to a deterministic packing theorem that applies to finite state ensembles, including unequal priors. We develop the two-sender case first, with worked examples and figures, before treating any fixed number of senders. Sharper finite-error guarantees for the same decoder are developed separately, with sharp bounds for two specified steps of the analysis rather than a claim of globally optimal decoding. Applications recover known achievable rates for unassisted and entanglement-assisted classical communication, distributed classical compression with quantum side information, and coherent-state communication through a beamsplitter or passive multiport device. The common proof makes the geometric mechanism and its quantitative consequences available without repeating the construction for each application.

Mark M. Wilde

item.title: [13★] From Syndromes to Computation: A General Framework for Logical Operations in Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
item.author: Hunter Nelson, ..., Sophia E. Economou, Edwin Barnes
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 13 ★

Authors: Hunter Nelson, ..., Sophia E. Economou, Edwin Barnes

arXiv ID: 2610.17612 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires error-correcting codes that not only protect quantum information but also support useful logical operations with practical physical realizations. Here we develop a general framework in which the stabilizer syndromes of commuting Pauli rotations directly organize logical-gate design. We derive an exact codespace-preservation condition valid at arbitrary rotation angles, providing a common stabilizer-level description for CSS and non-CSS codes and for both Clifford and non-Clifford operations. A particularly useful equal-syndrome specialization reduces Clifford gate design to stabilizer factorization, yields a general generator weight bound of ⌈d/2⌉\lceil d/2\rceil for distance-dd codes, and systematically extends to logical rotations higher in the Clifford hierarchy. Applied to bivariate-bicycle (BB) and non-CSS Mirror qLDPC codes, the framework gives explicit low-weight Clifford and controlled-phase gates. Our implementations yield new low-weight gates, including an addressed TT gate on the [[16,4,4]][[16,4,4]] BB code, TT-type rotations on the [[64,8,8]][[64,8,8]] BB code, and CCZ-, CS-, and TT-type operations on the [[36,6,6]][[36,6,6]] Mirror code. We also develop analytic constructions using Clifford algebra bases, which turn the syndrome constraints into explicit algebraic relations and provide a systematic route to logical addressability. We use this approach to analytically construct addressed CNOT, SWAP, controlled, and CCZ-type gates on recursive hypercube codes. An independent construction on middle quantum Reed--Muller codes yields Cr{}^rZ gates that saturate the equal-syndrome weight bound. These results establish stabilizer syndromes as a constructive link between the stabilizer structure of a quantum code, the logical computations it can directly support, and the fault-tolerance properties of their physical realizations.

Hunter Nelson, ..., Sophia E. Economou, Edwin Barnes

item.title: [13★] Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
item.author: Piotr Ćwikliński
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 13 ★

Authors: Piotr Ćwikliński

arXiv ID: 2610.16351 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

An isolated quantum system evolves reversibly, yet a small subsystem can lose nearly all information about its initial state. Conserved quantities may retain some of this information, depending on how strongly they overlap with local observables. Here we consider a subsystem in an arbitrary initial state coupled to a maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square equilibration error, maximised over window origins, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation, with the stationary part subtracted. A correlation record over a finite interval therefore controls the equilibration error in every interval of the same length. The result allows arbitrary degeneracies of energies and gaps. We apply it to two static Hamiltonian families. For fixed spin subsystems in the one-particle sector of a bounded-range periodic clock, fixed-accuracy thermalisation is guaranteed on windows that grow only slightly faster than linearly with system size, despite exponentially small positive energies. A random commuting model with logarithmic interaction range retains an extensive set of conserved observables. Its expected mean-square error is bounded by a finite-size term and an inverse-time term. The inverse-time dependence is unavoidable because of the initial transient. These examples show how local relaxation can coexist with exact conservation laws and a finely spaced spectrum.

Piotr Ćwikliński

item.title: [12★] Probe Signatures of Quantum Chaos with Quantum Sensing
item.author: Isaías Vallejo-Fabila, Jing Yang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 12 ★

Authors: Isaías Vallejo-Fabila, Jing Yang

arXiv ID: 2610.16181 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The spectral form factor (SFF), which is the Fourier transform of the two-point spectral correlation, is a fundamental diagnostics of quantum chaos. Nevertheless, its experimental detection in quantum many-body systems was less unexplored until recently. Here, we establish a relationship between the SFF with the quantum Fisher information (QFI) by means of quantum sensing protocols. Furthermore, when the eigenvalues and eigenstates of the disordered Hamiltonian are statistically independent, we prove that QFI is typical both in short and long timescales while numerics suggest that it is also typical at intermediate timescales, which ensures self-averaging of QFI. The self-averaging property renders the experimental measurement of QFI with our protocol less noisy in contrast with the direct measurement of SFF which is known to be non-self-averaging. Our results reveal an intriguing connection between quantum noise and the signatures of quantum chaos.

Isaías Vallejo-Fabila, Jing Yang

item.title: [10★] Error-Corrected QRAM Queries with One-Fault-Tolerant \textttCSWAP Gates
item.author: Shifan Xu, ..., Steven M. Girvin, Yongshan Ding
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 10 ★

Authors: Shifan Xu, ..., Steven M. Girvin, Yongshan Ding

arXiv ID: 2610.17185 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum random-access memory (QRAM) enables coherent queries to classical data. However, the O(N)O(N)qubits required for a memory with N=2nN=2^naddresses make QRAM appear vulnerable to noise. Though bucket-brigade routing provides intrinsic noise resilience to reduce the error in QRAM, improving the fidelity of QRAM queries is still an important and challenging problem. We introduce a low-overhead protection framework for bucket-brigade QRAM with two complementary components. First, we propose a one-fault-tolerant repeat-until-success logical controlled-SWAP gate using the [[4,2,2]][[4,2,2]]code under erasure noise channel. Interleaved erasure checks and local recovery correct every single erasure, so the leading logical failure probability is second order in the physical erasure error rates. Second, we exploit validity constraints of bucket-brigade routing to define local parity checks directly on the router states, without adding extra data qubits to create code redundancy. Under bit-flip noise, minimum-weight perfect matching with noiseless syndrome measurements corrects single interior faults, while open spatial boundaries retain a first-order contribution in the residual bit-flip rate. Monte Carlo simulations confirm quadratic suppression for the protected controlled-SWAP and improved depth scaling for decoded QRAM router-state snapshots. The two codes admit a concatenated realization in which the inner code supplies erasure protection and the outer code optionally corrects interior logical bit flips. Together, these results show how routing constraints and a protected non-Clifford routing gate can improve QRAM reliability under biased and erasure-dominant noise.

Shifan Xu, ..., Steven M. Girvin, Yongshan Ding

item.title: [10★] Breakdown of thermalization in quantum spin systems with long-range interactions
item.author: Filippo Caleca, Fabio Mezzacapo, Tommaso Roscilde
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 10 ★

Authors: Filippo Caleca, Fabio Mezzacapo, Tommaso Roscilde

arXiv ID: 2610.15530 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum thermalization of closed systems -- i.e. the relaxation of local properties to their thermodynamic value along the Hamiltonian evolution -- is generically expected in non-integrable systems at finite energy density. In this work we show that quantum spin systems with at least one spin component coupled through long-range ferromagnetic interactions, and a second spin component coupled to a field, cannot in general thermalize to a paramagnetic state whenever they have a finite, negative energy per spin. The long-range interactions we consider decay as a power law of the distance, ∼r−α\sim r^{-\alpha} with α<d\alpha < d, where dd is the number of spatial dimensions of the system. The lack of thermalization is generic to an infinite family of Hamiltonians, and it is not associated to any form of integrability. It can instead be understood by the anomalous features of the thermodynamics of the system in the paramagnetic phase, which cannot be reflected in the properties of the eigenstates. This leads to a breakdown of eigenstate typicality and of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Interestingly, the non-thermal states emerging at long times in the dynamics display long-range multipartite entanglement, elevating the breakdown of thermalization to a resource.

Filippo Caleca, Fabio Mezzacapo, Tommaso Roscilde

item.title: [9★] Nearly Optimal Quantum Sample Complexity of Learning Fourier-Sparse Boolean Functions
item.author: Zekun Ye
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 9 ★

Authors: Zekun Ye

arXiv ID: 2610.17648 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We study the number of uniform quantum examples needed to exactly learn a Boolean function with at most kk nonzero Fourier coefficients. We give a learner with near-optimal ˜O(k)\widetilde{O}(k) sample complexity independent of the input length nn. The learner uses only separate measurements of individual examples. This improves the previous O(k3/2log2k)O(k^{3/2}\log^2 k) upper bound (Arunachalam, Chakraborty, Lee, Paraashar, and de Wolf, 2021). The main ingredient is a candidate set formed by symmetric differences of subsets from independent groups of Fourier samples. A multilinear majority polynomial combines unbiased random approximations into an accurate witness whose Fourier support lies in this set. Granularity then forces the set to contain the entire Fourier support, including subsets never directly sampled. For comparison, we derive the tight classical sample complexity Θ(nk)\Theta(nk) by combining known sparse-recovery and lower-bound results.

Zekun Ye

item.title: [8★] Relative-Entropy Geometry and Convergence in Nonconvex Wiretap Optimization
item.author: Farzin Salek, Masahito Hayashi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Farzin Salek, Masahito Hayashi

arXiv ID: 2610.18785 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We develop and analyze an entropic descent method for a nonconvex optimization problem on probability simplices arising in classical and quantum secure communication. The optimization variables describe a randomized encoder, allowing its input distribution and stochastic preprocessing to be optimized jointly. An exact relative-entropy identity yields a channel-independent majorization bound and an explicit mirror-descent iteration with a fixed unit step size. We establish quantitative descent, convergence of objective values, and stationarity of accumulation points on their support faces for arbitrary finite classical channels, without assuming degradedness or less noisiness. For strictly positive transition matrices, a square-root parametrization and a Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz argument establish finite length of the transformed trajectory and convergence of the entire sequence, including limits on the simplex boundary. For less-noisy channels, a restricted convex formulation admits global convergence with an explicit O(1/t)O(1/t)objective-error bound. We extend the relative-entropy construction to noncommuting quantum outputs and derive monotone alternating updates for covariant encoders, including correlated preprocessing over a fixed block. Numerical experiments compare the method with analytic benchmarks and constrained optimization, reveal multiple attracting values, and demonstrate strict improvements from stochastic preprocessing.

Farzin Salek, Masahito Hayashi

item.title: [8★] Moving quantum sensors
item.author: Evan Zhang, ..., Andrew M. Childs, Alexey V. Gorshkov
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Evan Zhang, ..., Andrew M. Childs, Alexey V. Gorshkov

arXiv ID: 2610.17176 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We investigate whether controlled motion of a quantum sensor offers a metrological advantage in a field-detection task. We consider a localized field of known strength BB occupying an unknown contiguous region making up a fraction 1/N1/N of the total search space, with a qubit sensor controlled for a total time TT to maximize the probability of detecting the field. We study the regime in which the characteristic timescale of the field is slow compared to the time to move the sensor between any two regions, and we distinguish classical motion, where the sensor follows a definite trajectory, from quantum motion, where the sensor can be in a coherent superposition of locations. For a single classically moving sensor, we derive an optimal multi-stop protocol and obtain the exact maximum detection probability. Allowing coherent spatial superposition maps the single-sensor problem onto Hamiltonian search and reduces the interrogation time for successfully detecting the field from Θ(N/B)\Theta(N/B) to Θ(√N/B)\Theta(\sqrt{N}/B). We then extend the problem to MM sensors and identify a hierarchy of optimal time scalings for constant success probability determined by the available spatial and inter-sensor quantum resources. Unentangled coherently moving sensors achieve T=Θ(√N/M/B)T=\Theta(\sqrt{N/M}/B) by searching disjoint regions in parallel, while entanglement among the sensors can further enhance the effective field coupling and achieve T=Θ(√N/(MB))T=\Theta(\sqrt{N}/(MB)). Matching lower bounds establish the optimality of these scalings in the presence of arbitrary controls and ancilla systems. Our results separate the roles of classical motion, spatial coherence, and entanglement in spatial field detection.

Evan Zhang, ..., Andrew M. Childs, Alexey V. Gorshkov

item.title: [8★] Magic-Free Certification of Logical Error Rates in Universal Fault-Tolerant Circuits
item.author: Gebrat Porta-San Miguel, Shahram Panahiyan, Dieter Jaksch
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Gebrat Porta-San Miguel, Shahram Panahiyan, Dieter Jaksch

arXiv ID: 2610.16401 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

As quantum hardware enters the fault-tolerant regime, algorithms are beginning to be executed on encoded qubits, yet scalable certification of how well they run remains an open problem. Here we introduce magic-free certification, a certification protocol for universal fault-tolerant circuits that consumes no magic, the resource that generally places them beyond efficient classical simulation and is by far the most expensive element of a fault-tolerant computation. The protocol is code- and decoder-agnostic, runs interleaved with the target circuit on the same device, and has a sample complexity that grows linearly with the number of logical qubits and non-Clifford gates while remaining decoupled from the logical error rate itself. Given a predefined error tolerance p∗Lp_L^*, the protocol determines at a chosen confidence level whether the device executes the target circuit at a logical error rate below p∗Lp_L^*. The method relies on trap circuits, copies of the target with every magic state replaced by a stabilizer state, whose outcomes are deterministic and which, being indistinguishable from the target to stochastic Pauli noise, fail at the same rate. We illustrate the protocol in Steane-code simulations of a magic state injection gadget and a quantum Fourier transform.

Gebrat Porta-San Miguel, Shahram Panahiyan, Dieter Jaksch

item.title: [7★] Gaussian entanglement and quantum communication: geodesic optimization and multimode bounds
item.author: Hemant K. Mishra, Mark M. Wilde
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 7 ★

Authors: Hemant K. Mishra, Mark M. Wilde

arXiv ID: 2610.18827 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Loss and noise limit the use of light to distribute entanglement, transmit quantum information, and establish secret keys. Gaussian states have a compact description in terms of means and covariance matrices, but their entanglement still requires global optimization. We develop a framework for computing Gaussian-restricted versions of the relative entropy of entanglement and Rains entanglement. An integral representation reveals a convex geometry under matrix geometric means and reduces Gaussian Rains entanglement to relative entropy minimized over Gaussian states with positive partial transpose. We obtain unique optimal reference states and additivity for independent Gaussian input states. Our convex-majorization algorithm has an explicit geometric convergence rate, uniform in the faithful regularization parameter and valid for pure input states. Controlled numerical integration and approximate convex subproblem solutions give a bit-complexity bound that is polynomial in accuracy bits for each fixed rational input covariance matrix, with explicit dependence on covariance size. These calculations bound extractable entanglement and, through the relative entropy of entanglement, extractable secret key. Teleportation simulation, energy allocation, and a convex optimization of passive-basis loss cores give bounds on quantum and private communication under an input-energy constraint, allowing arbitrary two-way classically assisted protocols. Two- and three-mode examples compare the bounds with achievable rates, including matching pure-loss benchmarks. Finally, we separate the Gaussian-restricted quantities from their unrestricted counterparts and give a photon-number truncation method with controlled error for computing the latter.

Hemant K. Mishra, Mark M. Wilde

item.title: [7★] EFI⇔1PRS\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}
item.author: Rishabh Batra
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 7 ★

Authors: Rishabh Batra

arXiv ID: 2610.18799 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. Together with the equivalence of statistically verifiable one-way state generators and commitments proved by Batra and Jain [BJ24], this gives a quantum analogue of the classical equivalence between one-way functions, commitments, and pseudorandom generators.

Rishabh Batra

item.title: [7★] Methods for Automated Equivalence Checking of Quantum Error-Correction Codes
item.author: Maxie Bichmann, Ludwig Schmid, Robert Wille
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 7 ★

Authors: Maxie Bichmann, Ludwig Schmid, Robert Wille

arXiv ID: 2610.18218 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum error-correction code and circuit construction is an active field of research, motivating automated methods for identifying equivalent designs. We develop and evaluate automated strategies for deciding whether two descriptions of quantum error-correction codes are equivalent under specified transformations. We formalize permutation equivalence for stabilizer and CSS codes and local-Clifford equivalence for stabilizer codes within a unified framework that separates physical from representation freedom. We develop three decision strategies (group-action search, isomorphism-based methods, and constraint solving), together with invariants and signatures for preprocessing. The empirical evaluation shows that no paradigm dominates across equivalence notions, code families, and parameter ranges. We therefore combine their complementary strengths in input-dependent hybrid checkers following a staged Refute-Refine-Decide architecture. Mean hybrid runtimes remain below 10 s for most evaluated structured-code cases with n≤37n \leq 37; for inequivalent code instances with n=144n=144, they are about 310 s for permutation and 16 s for local-Clifford equivalence.

Maxie Bichmann, Ludwig Schmid, Robert Wille

item.title: [7★] Bootstrapping Classical and Quantum Query Lower Bounds for Finding Tarski Fixed Points
item.author: Tongyang Li, ..., Ziyi Yang, Xingyu Zhao
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 7 ★

Authors: Tongyang Li, ..., Ziyi Yang, Xingyu Zhao

arXiv ID: 2610.16209 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The Tarski fixed-point problem asks for a fixed point of a monotone map on a kk-dimensional grid lattice of width nn and has applications in game theory, economics, and verification. Substantial gaps remain between the known upper and lower bounds on its quantum query complexity. We prove two hardness bootstrapping theorems for quantum query lower bounds. Starting from a hard instance family whose instances have pair-wise incomparable unique fixed points, and a lower bound established by the nonnegative adversary method, we bootstrap this lower bound by (i) a factor of Ω(t)\Omega(t) when the dimension is multiplied by tt and the width remains unchanged, and (ii) a factor of Ω(logm)\Omega(\log m) when the width is multiplied by mm and the dimension is doubled. Applying these theorems, we obtain three consequences: (i) an Ω(klog2n)\Omega(k\log^2 n) lower bound for k≥4k\geq 4, improving previously best-known classical and quantum lower bounds; (ii) for every fixed constant α>0\alpha>0, there exists a constant δ(α)>0\delta(\alpha)>0 such that Qϵ(Tarski(n,k))=Ω(knδ(α))Q_\epsilon(\text{Tarski}(n,k))=\Omega(kn^{\delta(\alpha)}) whenever k>nαk>n^\alpha, and in particular, an Ω(kn0.0072)\Omega(kn^{0.0072}) lower bound for k>n2/203k>n^{2/203}, the first lower bound with simultaneous linear dependence on the dimension and polynomial dependence on the width; and (iii) a superpolynomial lower bound of (k/logk)Ω(logk)(k/\log k)^{\Omega(\log k)} for exponentially wide grids, where n=2Θ(k)n=2^{\Theta(k)}. The last result rules out a route to polynomial-time algorithms for simple stochastic games and ARRIVAL through generic polynomial-query black-box Tarski solvers.

Tongyang Li, ..., Ziyi Yang, Xingyu Zhao

item.title: [7★] Local-dimension-invariant low-density parity-check stabilizer codes
item.author: Md. Shahinul Islam, Aaryan Reza, Lane G. Gunderman
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 7 ★

Authors: Md. Shahinul Islam, Aaryan Reza, Lane G. Gunderman

arXiv ID: 2610.15893 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The protection of quantum information in systems leveraging more than two basis states (qudits) is an ongoing challenge. A tool for transforming the plethora of qubit stabilizer codes into qudit stabilizer codes is the local-dimension-invariant (LDI) extension to the stabilizer formalism. A drawback of the LDI method is that generally in order to ensure the distance of the resultant code is at least preserved the newly selected local-dimension will need to be any prime bigger than a large cutoff value. In this work we consider the repercussions of this large cutoff value, then by focusing on quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes we are able to bring down this cutoff value. Notably, we are able to reduce it in some cases to the initial local-dimension and for arbitrary CSS qubit-derived codes to singly exponential in dd with no dependence on the number of logicals kk. This reduces the size of the caveat in LDI forms in their distance preservation condition.

Md. Shahinul Islam, Aaryan Reza, Lane G. Gunderman

item.title: [6★] Genuine Information Backflow Requires Noncommuting Initial System States
item.author: Abdullah Alsharari, Francesco Buscemi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Abdullah Alsharari, Francesco Buscemi

arXiv ID: 2610.15430 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) equation, a cornerstone of open-system theory, describes Markovian semigroup dynamics in which information about the initial preparation cannot revive. Beyond this regime, information revivals are widely interpreted as backflow from a non-Markovian environment. However, a decrease followed by an increase in information retrievable from the system need not imply that information has returned from the environment [PRX Quantum 6, 020316 (2025)]. It may instead arise from noise correlations unrelated to the system's initial preparation, carried by inert degrees of freedom that never interact with the system and therefore cannot mediate backflow. Such revivals are called extrinsic; genuine backflow is reserved for revivals that cannot be explained this way. The framework developed in that work, however, assumes access to arbitrary initial system states, an assumption often incompatible with physical constraints or limited experimental control. This leaves open which properties of the available preparations are necessary for an information revival to certify genuine backflow. Here we extend the framework to allow the description of restricted families of initial states and show that genuine backflow is possible only if the family contains noncommuting states. If all available states commute, as in a classical stochastic process, every revival can be explained by a suitable inert extension and is therefore extrinsic. Noncommutativity of the available system states is thus necessary for information revivals to provide an operational signature of environmental memory.

Abdullah Alsharari, Francesco Buscemi

item.title: [5★] How many switches does two-Hamiltonian universality require?
item.author: Matas Garbaravičius, Michael M. Wolf
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Matas Garbaravičius, Michael M. Wolf

arXiv ID: 2610.17826 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Any pair of sufficiently generic Hamiltonians on Cd\mathbb{C}^d generates the full unitary group, i.e., any W∈U(d)W\in U(d) can be synthesized to arbitrary precision by alternating between the two evolutions for suitably chosen durations. For any given pair of Hamiltonians, the minimal number of switches required to cover the entire group is at least dd and unbounded in general. Despite this, we show that it scales linearly in dd in expectation. Assuming that the two spectra are sufficiently generic, we derive constructive upper bounds on the minimal switching number as a function of the change-of-basis matrix between the two eigenbases. In particular, if this matrix has a column whose entries all have equal moduli, as for a complex Hadamard matrix, then 9d9d switches suffice to reach every unitary. To obtain these results, we construct a short exact representation of any unitary as a product of unitaries that are alternately diagonal in two given bases. All bounds are extended to non-generic spectra and bounded evolution times.

Matas Garbaravičius, Michael M. Wolf

item.title: [4★] Classical Communication Helps Single-Shot Quantum Compression
item.author: Omri Farber, Gilad Gour
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 4 ★

Authors: Omri Farber, Gilad Gour

arXiv ID: 2610.14785 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Free classical communication can yield an unbounded single-shot saving in quantum compression, even though it leaves the asymptotic rate of an i.i.d. source unchanged. At every fixed error in (0,1)(0,1), we exhibit sources whose unassisted compression cost is arbitrarily large, yet a single qubit suffices with classical communication and no preshared entanglement. We establish this separation by determining the exact optimal source fidelity for compression through an mm-dimensional noiseless quantum channel, with and without free classical communication, while preserving correlations with an inaccessible reference. Without classical assistance, the optimal fidelity is exactly the Ky Fan norm ‖ρ‖(m)\|\rho\|_{(m)}, the sum of the mm largest eigenvalues of the source state. With classical assistance, we obtain an explicit spectral threshold formula and a protocol attaining it. Classical communication strictly improves fidelity whenever mm is smaller than the source rank. The corresponding compression costs are two smoothed versions of the log-rank entropy, also called max-entropy: trace-distance smoothing under local operations and quadratic smoothing under LOCC. For i.i.d. copies of a fixed source with positive entropy variance, however, the two costs have identical first-, second-, and third-order asymptotic terms. For nonlattice spectra, we determine the constant-order advantage: classical communication saves log2(e)−1\log_2(e)-1 bits per block asymptotically, and the ratio of assisted to unassisted minimum communication dimensions converges to 2/e2/e.

Omri Farber, Gilad Gour

item.title: [3★] Benchmarking a randomized quantum algorithm for estimating expectation values of molecular observables
item.author: Anna Schroeder, ..., Michael Streif, Davide Vodola
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Anna Schroeder, ..., Michael Streif, Davide Vodola

arXiv ID: 2610.16379 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Randomized quantum algorithms for the estimation of expectation values of molecular observables offer a promising route to early fault-tolerant quantum advantage by trading circuit depth for an increased number of samples. However, this begs the question whether the resulting measurement overhead remains feasible for industrially relevant molecular systems. In this work, we benchmark the randomized sampling algorithm of Wang et al. [1] through numerical simulations on a hydrogen molecule and resource estimates for various active spaces of the cytochrome P450, an industry-relevant system in the pharmaceutical industry. Our numerical simulations reveal that the analytical error bounds significantly overestimate the actual sampling error, whereas the analytical bound on the required imaginary evolution time is comparatively tight, exceeding a direct DMRG estimate by roughly 44% for the active space where the comparison is feasible. The measurement overhead nevertheless remains prohibitively high: even for the smallest active spaces, the expectation-value estimation alone requires around 1010 samples, scaling to beyond 1015 for the largest active spaces considered. These results suggest that substantial improvements in measurement strategies or algorithmic scaling are necessary before randomized early-fault-tolerant algorithms become competitive for industrial quantum chemistry applications.

Anna Schroeder, ..., Michael Streif, Davide Vodola

item.title: [3★] Pathfinder-BP: A Low-Latency Recursive Decoder for Topological Codes
item.author: Stefano Tinelli, Francisco Lázaro, Francisco García Herrero
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Stefano Tinelli, Francisco Lázaro, Francisco García Herrero

arXiv ID: 2610.16375 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We propose Pathfinder-BP, a recursive decoder for topological quantum codes that combines belief propagation with controlled bit-flipping. An initial BP pass identifies and permanently fixes high-confidence errors. Upon convergence failure, the decoder recursively explores alternative error patterns by tentatively flipping low-confidence variables. On surface codes, Pathfinder-BP achieves a noise threshold and logical error rate comparable to minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM). A crucial advantage of Pathfinder-BP is its highly parallelizable structure, which yields a worst-case decoding latency quasi-linear in the code distance, making it a suitable candidate for low-latency hardware implementation.

Stefano Tinelli, Francisco Lázaro, Francisco García Herrero

item.title: [3★] Lifting an [n,k,d][n,k,d] Binary Linear Code to an [[n,k,d]][[n,k,d]] Quantum Stabilizer Code
item.author: Thamadathil Aswanth, Navin Kashyap
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Thamadathil Aswanth, Navin Kashyap

arXiv ID: 2610.14192 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The codeword stabilized (CWS) framework provides a systematic method for constructing quantum error correcting codes from a simple undirected graph and a classical code. When the underlying classical code is linear, the resulting quantum code is a stabilizer code. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which an arbitrary [n,k,d][n,k,d] classical binary linear code can be lifted to an [[n,k,d]][[n,k,d]] quantum stabilizer code using the CWS framework. We analyze the random CWS code constructed from a given [n,k,d][n,k,d] binary linear code C\mathcal{C} and an Erdős-Rényi random graph G(n,12)\mathrm{G}(n, \frac12). We establish a lower bound on the probability that the resulting quantum code preserves the minimum distance dd of the classical code. This probabilistic analysis yields a Gilbert-Varshamov-type condition on the n,k,dn,k,d parameters of the classical code that guarantees the existence of a graph resulting in a quantum code with the same n,k,dn,k,d parameters.

Thamadathil Aswanth, Navin Kashyap

item.title: [3★] Categorifying Quantum Spin Systems
item.author: Matthew Yu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Matthew Yu

arXiv ID: 2610.14165 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We develop a homotopical framework for understanding the space of quantum spin systems based on topological nn-nets, which assign associative unital algebras to local regions in an nn-dimensional space in a manner that captures the locality structure of the underlying lattice theories. The net-theoretic perspective admits a natural categorification, in which the category of topological nn-nets carries the structure of a higher Morita category. Moreover, the nets of greatest physical interest form a Karoubi-complete subcategory that shares many of the characteristic structural features of the category of finite TQFTs. Our main result identifies the group of locality-preserving symmetries of (3+1)-dimensional quantum spin systems (i.e. quantum cellular automata modulo stabilization, finite-depth quantum circuits, and translations) with the full Witt group of nondegenerate braided fusion categories, thereby answering a question posed by Haah.

Matthew Yu

item.title: [2★] PPVM: A Circuit Simulation Framework for Digital Twins of Quantum Processors
item.author: Xiu-Zhe Luo, ..., Stefan Ostermann, Sheng-Tao Wang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Xiu-Zhe Luo, ..., Stefan Ostermann, Sheng-Tao Wang

arXiv ID: 2610.18225 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum computers are approaching the early fault-tolerant regime. Verifying the next generation of quantum hardware requires joint emulation of the quantum processor, hardware noise, and classical control and decoding logic. We introduce the Programmable Pauli Virtual Machine (PPVM), an open-source framework for digital twins of quantum processors. PPVM unifies Pauli propagation and generalized tableau simulation under a common abstraction within a single virtual machine. Its bytecode supports arbitrary classical control flow, with measurement-conditioned feed-forward available in the generalized tableau backend. For neutral-atom hardware, we derive independent and correlated atom-loss channels and integrate them into both backends. We demonstrate loss-aware magic state distillation on over a thousand physical qubits and integration with classical decoding through Bloqade QEC Studio.

Xiu-Zhe Luo, ..., Stefan Ostermann, Sheng-Tao Wang

item.title: [2★] Distance Prediction for Quantum Codes
item.author: Nadav Schneider, Eliya Nachmani
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Nadav Schneider, Eliya Nachmani

arXiv ID: 2610.18130 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The distance of a quantum code is a fundamental metric that dictates its error-correction capability. While quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) families such as Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes offer a promising pathway to low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computing, computing their distance is challenging. Current exact solvers and even search heuristics that provide a distance upper bound suffer from severe computational bottlenecks, restricting the discovery of optimal codes. In this paper, we construct a dataset of BB codes with corresponding distance upper bounds obtained through high-budget heuristic searches. We introduce BB-Net, an attention-based neural network architecture for predicting the distance of BB codes. It achieves 96.39% accuracy on the reference distances in the test set, compared with 94.86% for state-of-the-art heuristics with a budget of up to 10410^{4} times more computational runtime. On a subset with certified exact distances, BB-Net achieves 98.94%. By relieving the distance-calculation bottleneck, BB-Net enables faster screening of large code spaces, particularly in ML-driven search pipelines, and thereby can accelerate the discovery of novel quantum error-correcting codes, an important capability for advancing scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing. Our code is publicly available: https://github.com/NadavSc/BBNet

Nadav Schneider, Eliya Nachmani

item.title: [2★] Optimal Lower Bound on the Sample Complexity of Coherent Classical Shadows for Mixed States
item.author: Pavel Svetlichnyy
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Pavel Svetlichnyy

arXiv ID: 2610.18031 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We study coherent classical shadows protocols for an unknown dd-dimensional quantum state of rank at most rr, allowing an arbitrary joint measurement on all available copies. For observables with operator norm at most one and centered squared Frobenius norm at most FF, we study the minumum number of copies TT needed for the protocol to successed with propbability 1−δ1 - \delta. We prove a lower bound on TT, that depends both on δ\delta and the number MM of post-measurement observables. Denoting ℓ=max{log(2M),log(1/δ)}\ell=\max\{\log(2M),\log(1/\delta)\}, we show that T=Ω(min{√rFℓε,(Fℓ)2/3ε4/3}+ℓε2)T=\Omega\left(\min\left\{\frac{\sqrt{rF\ell}}{\varepsilon},\frac{(F\ell)^{2/3}}{\varepsilon^{4/3}}\right\}+\frac{\ell}{\varepsilon^2}\right) under the mild assumption log(2M)≲dmin{r,F}\log(2M)\lesssim d\min\{r,F\}. The lower bound nearly matches the known upper bound and matches the conjectural strengthening of the known upper bound. The proof is inspired by the framework of the proof of the lower bound for Boolean Hidden Matching. We develop a Gaussian-lift noise kernel that transfers forward and reverse Gaussian hypercontractivity to the Grassmannian, allowing us to bound the distinguishing advantage in an auxiliary game with a revealed query observable. We use Schur--Weyl structure and posterior moment bounds to control arbitrary coherent measurements on the source side.

item.title: [2★] QEDIA: Quantum Program Verification in Lean
item.author: Yuanjie Ren, ..., Yidi Qi, Mingsheng Ying
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Yuanjie Ren, ..., Yidi Qi, Mingsheng Ying

arXiv ID: 2610.17708 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Practical quantum programs interleave quantum and classical computation: classical data shape the quantum operations that are performed, and measurement outcomes shape the classical computation that follows. Formal verification of such programs in a proof assistant requires mechanizing a program logic that handles this interplay consistently at every level, from the mathematics of quantum mechanics, through program syntax and semantics, to specifications and proof rules. Such mechanizations, along with the program proofs built on them, typically require substantial manual effort. We present QEDIA, a framework for verifying quantum programs with classical variables in Lean 4. At its foundation is an open library that formalizes the quantum Hoare logic QHL+ across all these levels and proves the logic sound for both partial and total correctness. We construct the library and the program proofs, under human supervision, using an LLM-based prover agent, whose general-purpose core we extend for quantum program verification. We illustrate QEDIA with verified programs including the quantum Fourier transform, phase estimation, repeat-until-success circuits, and Hamiltonian simulation.

Yuanjie Ren, ..., Yidi Qi, Mingsheng Ying

item.title: [2★] Chromatic Block-Gibbs p-Bit Decoding of QLDPC Codes
item.author: Mert Gökduman, Cyril Guyot, Henry D. Pfister
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Mert Gökduman, Cyril Guyot, Henry D. Pfister

arXiv ID: 2610.17520 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We introduce a parallel decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes based on probabilistic bits (p-bits), tunable stochastic binary units controlled by local fields. The idea is that predicted error configurations, interpreted as explanations of the observed syndrome, are updated stochastically using local Gibbs conditionals, while a progressively strengthened parity penalty drives the search toward syndrome-valid configurations. A coloring of the decoding graph enables parallel block updates, and independent replicas and restarts provide trajectory diversity. The best candidate encountered during the search is returned, mirroring the candidate-selection strategy of recent ensemble decoders. At the stated update budgets, the resulting logical error rates are on par with leading decoders under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise. While the total number of variable resamplings can be substantially larger than the message-update count of BP-based alternatives, the numerical results establish constraint-annealed p-bit dynamics as a competitive stochastic alternative for QLDPC decoding and motivate further study of hardware-native implementations.

Mert Gökduman, Cyril Guyot, Henry D. Pfister

item.title: [2★] Turning a superconducting diode into a Feynman ratchet to realize a nanoscale heat engine
item.author: Konstantinos Kontogeorgiou, ..., Géraldine Haack, Fabian Hassler
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Konstantinos Kontogeorgiou, ..., Géraldine Haack, Fabian Hassler

arXiv ID: 2610.17257 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Feynman's ratchet illustrates how work can be extracted from thermal fluctuations in the presence of two heat baths at different temperatures. While some experimental realizations of the ratchet effect have been studied, most lack miniaturization, which is important for some applications. Here, we propose a physical implementation of Feynman's ratchet based on Josephson junctions exhibiting the superconducting diode effect. This setup functions as a heat engine that generates work solely from a temperature gradient via thermal fluctuations. We analyze its output power and efficiency, and, through the Seebeck coefficient, identify the conditions under which the device operates in reverse, functioning instead as a Peltier cooler.

Konstantinos Kontogeorgiou, ..., Géraldine Haack, Fabian Hassler

item.title: [2★] Fermionic non-Gaussianity via computable measures and experimentally accessible bounds
item.author: Leela Ganesh Chandra Lakkaraju, Naga Dileep Varikuti, Philipp Hauke
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Leela Ganesh Chandra Lakkaraju, Naga Dileep Varikuti, Philipp Hauke

arXiv ID: 2610.17219 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Interacting fermions owe both their non-trivial correlations and their computational power to their departure from Gaussianity. Yet, quantifying that departure geometrically faces two challenges: the Gaussian manifold is non-convex, and perturbative treatments are confined to weak interactions. Here, we introduce a geometric measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity, the fidelity distance of a target state to the manifold of fermionic Gaussian states. We construct an iteration formalism to numerically access it, applicable also at strong coupling. Further, we prove a sharpened operator Jensen inequality, of interest in its own right. We use it to derive a witness that involves only two- and four-point fermionic correlators. Numerical benchmarks on the one-dimensional Fermi--Hubbard model show that the quality of the witness improves with system size and, for strong coupling, is tighter than antiflatness. Our results open a scalable route to charting non-Gaussianity of strongly-interacting fermionic quantum simulators.

Leela Ganesh Chandra Lakkaraju, Naga Dileep Varikuti, Philipp Hauke

item.title: [2★] Revealing topological protection through unprotected operations in a Majorana parity qubit
item.author: Sebastian Miles, ..., Leo P. Kouwenhoven, Michael Wimmer
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Sebastian Miles, ..., Leo P. Kouwenhoven, Michael Wimmer

arXiv ID: 2610.17198 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A recent experiment reported coherent parity oscillations between minimal Kitaev chains, demonstrating a Majorana parity qubit (arXiv:2607.09511). Operations on this qubit are controlled by coupling two Kitaev chains and are intrinsically unprotected against noise in the coupling strength. Here we show how the exponential protection in the underlying chains can nevertheless be revealed through unprotected qubit operations. To this end, we develop an analytical theory of quasistatic dephasing for two coupled NN-site Kitaev chains at the sweet spot. In Rabi experiments, protection can be resolved by adapting the operating point with chain length: depending on the coupling architecture, it appears as an exponentially increasing optimized number of coherent oscillations or as a longer coherence time. Ramsey experiments show an exponentially increasing coherence time, provided the chains can be sufficiently decoupled. Our analytical theory takes into account the non-Gaussian splitting statistics of the Kitaev chains, allowing us to quantitatively predict the scaling with chain length. Moreover, we determine how residual noise and imperfections limit the range of chain lengths over which this scaling can be observed. Our results show how qubit dynamics can be used to probe Majorana protection in experimentally realistic devices.

Sebastian Miles, ..., Leo P. Kouwenhoven, Michael Wimmer

item.title: [2★] Bosonic unstructured search: quantum enhancement without entanglement
item.author: Yu-Xin Wang, ..., Alexey V. Gorshkov, Mohammad Hafezi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Yu-Xin Wang, ..., Alexey V. Gorshkov, Mohammad Hafezi

arXiv ID: 2610.17163 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We consider unstructured search using multimode bosonic quantum systems under energy constraints. The task is to locate an unknown marked mode among NN possibilities using arbitrary control, subject to a time-averaged mean-boson-number budget nb≫1n_{{\text{b}}}\gg 1. We analyze a continuous-time phase-shift oracle of strength B0B_{0}, with cost given by the total oracle time, and a discrete oracle with fixed phase ϕ0\phi_{0}, with cost given by the number of queries. We give algorithms that identify the target with query complexity O(√N/nbB0)O(\sqrt{N}/{n_{{\text{b}}}}B_{0}) for continuous-time oracles or O(√N/nb|sin(ϕ0/2)|)O(\sqrt{N}/n_{{\text{b}}} |{\sin(\phi_{0}/{2})}|) for discrete oracles with nb|sin(ϕ0/2)|=O(1)n_{{\text{b}}} |{\sin(\phi_{0}/{2})}|=O(1). In contrast, for discrete oracles with nb|sin(ϕ0/2)|=Ω(1)n_{{\text{b}}} |{\sin(\phi_{0}/{2})}|=\Omega(1), we provide an algorithm using O(max{1,√N/nb|sin(ϕ0/2)|})O(\max\{1,\sqrt{N/n_{{\text{b}}}|{\sin(\phi_{0}/{2})}|}\}) queries. We also prove matching lower bounds on the query complexity, showing that these algorithms are asymptotically optimal. Furthermore, we show that, in the absence of loss, non-Gaussianity is necessary to achieve the optimal joint query scaling in NN and nbn_{{\text{b}}}, but entanglement is not. Under uniform boson loss at rate γ\gamma, we prove a query lower bound of Ω(γN/nbB20)\Omega ( \gamma N / n _{{\text{b}}} B_{0}^{2} ), attained for γ=Ω(B0√nb/N)\gamma = \Omega(B_{0} \sqrt{n _{{\text{b}}}/N}) using coherent-state probes. Finally, we propose experimental implementations using multipass optical microscopy or superconducting circuits as potential routes to speeding up imaging or device calibration with a low boson-number budget.

Yu-Xin Wang, ..., Alexey V. Gorshkov, Mohammad Hafezi

item.title: [2★] Deterministic preparation of squeezed and non-Gaussian states in coupled qubit-boson systems
item.author: Fengquan Zhang, ..., Zhiyuan Lin, Tim Byrnes
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Fengquan Zhang, ..., Zhiyuan Lin, Tim Byrnes

arXiv ID: 2610.16207 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Deterministic preparation of bosonic resource states is a central task in continuous-variable quantum information processing and quantum metrology. Here we develop a measurement-based imaginary time evolution (MITE) protocol for preparing squeezed and non-Gaussian states. The protocol combines ancilla-mediated weak measurements of the Hamiltonian with a conditional phase rotation that suppresses excited state trapping and stabilizes convergence toward the ground state. The method is potentially applicable in hybrid discrete variable-continuous variable (DV-CV) platforms, where the qubit acts as the measurement readout. We demonstrate deterministic convergence over a broad range of parameters and show that the performance degradation near the stability boundary is governed by the shrinking Bogoliubov quasiparticle gap. The same framework also extends to non-Gaussian bosonic resource states, including Schrödinger cat states and excited states of the single-mode squeezing Hamiltonian, which display Wigner negativity. The squeezed states remain robust under bosonic loss over experimentally relevant regimes.

Fengquan Zhang, ..., Zhiyuan Lin, Tim Byrnes

item.title: [2★] Sequential optimization for orbital-optimized variational quantum eigensolvers
item.author: Hiromichi Hayashi, Takeshi Sato
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Hiromichi Hayashi, Takeshi Sato

arXiv ID: 2610.16032 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Orbital optimization within the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) framework is useful for improving active-space quality and accurately capturing electron correlation with shallow quantum circuits. The orbital-optimized unitary coupled cluster (OO-UCC) method [W. Mizukami et al., Phys. Rev. Res. 2, 033421 (2020)], in its original formulation, employs the orbital gradient and Hessian in a Newton--Laphson procedure. In this study, we propose sequential orbital-optimized unitary coupled cluster doubles (SOO-UCCD), extending the gradient-free sequential minimal optimization approach [K. M. Nakanishi et al., Phys. Rev. Res. 2, 043158 (2020)] to orbital rotation parameters. Based on the frequency structure implied by the algebraic properties of the orbital rotation generators, our method determines each orbital rotation angle from a nine-point energy profile. The energy landscape is evaluated by classically transforming the Hamiltonian integrals and contracting them with the reduced density matrices already measured for the VQE energy evaluation. This allows for orbital optimization without evaluating the orbital gradient or Hessian. By building on the core benefits of the OO-UCC framework, our method provides a gradient-free and hyperparameter-free orbital-optimization procedure. State-vector simulations for LiH in the STO-3G basis show that SOO-UCCD reproduces UCCSD-level accuracy along the bond-stretching curve and exhibits macro-iteration convergence comparable to that of L-BFGS-based orbital optimization.

Hiromichi Hayashi, Takeshi Sato

item.title: [2★] Scalable Exact Non-Pauli Noise Simulation for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
item.author: Yuewen Hou, Gokul Subramanian Ravi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Yuewen Hou, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

arXiv ID: 2610.15975 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Fault-tolerant quantum design relies on simulating noisy quantum error correction (QEC) circuits with hundreds to thousands of physical qubits and large circuit depths. High-throughput stabilizer simulators, such as Stim, are the de facto tools for this regime. However, these simulators typically support only Clifford gates and stochastic Pauli noise. As a result, more realistic device noise models-such as coherent control errors and thermal relaxation-are often approximated using Pauli Twirling. This replacement offers speed but can introduce inaccuracies. To address this, we propose QuasiStim for scalable exact QEC simulation of realistic noise, with QuasiFold as a compiler frontend and DeltaFrame as a sampling backend. QuasiFold lowers sampling overhead by merging equivalent non-Pauli sites in the quantum circuit. DeltaFrame samples the resulting stabilizer trajectories by reusing precomputed predicted references instead of resimulating the full tableau for each shot. QuasiFold can reduce the number of shots by over 100×100\times on bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes. Compared to a per-shot tableau simulator, DeltaFrame is 166×166\times--1331×1331\times faster on rotated surface-code memory under coherent RZR_Z noise as dd grows from 5 to 35. QuasiStim also makes the PTA bias measurable: the gap is non-negligible and varies with noise strength, decoder, and circuit schedule. QuasiStim will be open-sourced upon publication at https://github.com/isaachyw/QuasiStim

Yuewen Hou, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

item.title: [2★] Entanglement-Capability-Aware Finite-Bond Circuit Cutting for Distributed Quantum Computing
item.author: Weidong Liu, ..., Hengliang Guo, Qiang Chen
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Weidong Liu, ..., Hengliang Guo, Qiang Chen

arXiv ID: 2610.14580 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Distributed quantum computing distributes workloads that exceed a single processor's capacity across resource-constrained components. Circuit cutting enables this decomposition, but its effectiveness depends on partition choice. We present SACE, a Simulation-Aware Circuit Partitioning framework with Entanglement-Capability-Aware Screening. EP-Cost screens partitions using a parameter-dependent entanglement-capability proxy and native implementation cost. Under reconstruction constraints, finite-bond refinement selects the candidate that minimizes the worst-subcircuit discrepancy between normalized MPS simulations at bond dimensions χ\chi and 2χ2\chi. Across 14 exhaustively enumerated small-scale candidate spaces, EP-Cost-guided genetic algorithm selections attain co-optimal native quasiprobability decomposition (QPD) overhead, with a median within-circuit Spearman correlation of 0.9965 between EP-Cost and QPD overhead. At matched cut counts, EP-Cost reduces QPD overhead by 25.20×25.20\times and 16.89×16.89\times for 8- and 9-qubit QFT circuits, respectively, and improves sampled reconstruction. On 12-qubit approximate QFT, deterministic reconstruction reduces Pauli-observable mean absolute error in all six low-bond conditions and total-variation distance in five. With five cuts and 7,776 QPD terms, SACE is best on all four reconstruction metrics in four of six conditions. At 24 qubits, SACE improves exact-local QFT accuracy in all 30 instance-bond-dimension conditions against each EP-Cost-only, Kernighan-Lin, and spectral baseline. The 50-qubit QFT comparisons remain favorable as reference convergence improves. Weighted QAOA circuits provide complementary, more bond-sensitive evidence. Refinement benefits persist across three search methods; larger candidate panels improve the optimized proxy without guaranteeing lower exact-local error.

item.title: [1★] Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
item.author: Isabelle Franzen, ..., Zhi-Yuan Wei, Matteo Fadel
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Isabelle Franzen, ..., Zhi-Yuan Wei, Matteo Fadel

arXiv ID: 2610.18778 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Multimode mechanical resonators offer a large set of densely packed, long-lived bosonic modes within a single compact device, making them attractive for quantum simulation, quantum information processing, and quantum-enhanced sensing. Many such applications rely on multipartite entanglement, yet deterministic mechanical entanglement has so far been largely limited to pairs of modes. Here we demonstrate the deterministic and programmable preparation of multipartite entangled states among the phonon modes of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator coupled to a superconducting transmon qubit. By sequentially applying optimal-control-engineered isometries between the qubit and successive modes, we generate matrix product states of bond dimension two, including WW, Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ), and cluster states. We fully characterize these states via quantum state tomography and certify genuine multipartite entanglement among up to four modes. We further demonstrate correlated-noise sensing by exploiting the complementary decoherence responses of the stored WW and GHZ states, isolating inter-mode phase correlations from local decoherence and placing quantitative bounds on collective dephasing. Our results establish a scalable approach to preparing multipartite entangled states in mechanical systems, with promising applications in multiparameter sensing and tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects.

item.title: [1★] Quantum-enhanced mechanical sensing with machine-learning estimation
item.author: Finn Müßigbrodt, ..., Yiwen Chu, Matteo Fadel
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Finn Müßigbrodt, ..., Yiwen Chu, Matteo Fadel

arXiv ID: 2610.18776 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Massive mechanical oscillators couple directly to forces, accelerations and gravity, making them attractive probes of new physics and of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales. Pushing sensitivities beyond the standard quantum limit for signals of unknown phase requires non-Gaussian quantum states, whose metrological advantage has so far been confined to lighter systems such as trapped ions. Here we operate a microgram-scale acoustic mode of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator as a phase-insensitive quantum-enhanced sensor. A transmon qubit prepares the mode in Fock states of up to seven phonons by optimal control, and resolves its phonon-number distribution after interaction with a weak resonant signal. Bayesian analysis yields a Fisher information five times the vacuum value, a 7.0 dB gain in signal-amplitude sensitivity over any classical probe state, irrespective of its energy, currently limited by state preparation infidelities. We then train a neural network on the measured sensor response to perform Bayesian estimation without any analytical model of the system, showing the same sensitivity gain with half the systematic bias. Our results establish acoustic resonators prepared in non-Gaussian states as quantum-enhanced probes for high-frequency gravitational waves, dark matter and wave-function collapse.

item.title: [1★] Finite-energy two-way assisted capacities: Exact formulas for multimode loss and fading
item.author: Stefano Pirandola, Gaetana Spedalieri
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Stefano Pirandola, Gaetana Spedalieri

arXiv ID: 2610.18731 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We study quantum communication, entanglement distribution, and secret-key generation through multimode bosonic loss and fading channels, assisted by local quantum operations and two-way classical communication. Using sector teleportation, we determine the exact two-way quantum and secret-key capacities of multimode pure-loss channels under a mean photon-number constraint, allowing arbitrary adaptive quantum protocols. We extend these results to continuous frequency-dependent loss under a power constraint and identify the optimal allocation of photons among optical modes. For constant loss over an unlimited bandwidth, we obtain a closed-form capacity proportional to the square root of power. For randomly varying loss, we determine exact finite-energy capacities when the channel realization is publicly revealed, distinguishing knowledge before and after transmission. When fading remains unobserved, we derive capacity bounds and explicit formulas for an on/off channel. We also establish strong-converse bounds, with exact thresholds for the deterministic loss models considered here, observed fading, and unobserved fading with finitely many possible transmissivities. Under mean energy constraints, these thresholds generally exceed the corresponding finite-energy capacities. These results guide energy allocation and provide benchmarks for energy-constrained optical quantum communication with multimode signals and variable loss.

item.title: [1★] Experimental Realization of a C-Shunt Flux-Qubit Coupler for Controlled-Z Gates between Transmons
item.author: Weiping Yuan, ..., Zhongcheng Xiang, Dongning Zheng
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Weiping Yuan, ..., Zhongcheng Xiang, Dongning Zheng

arXiv ID: 2610.18477 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Fast entangling gates and low-interaction idling require distinct operating conditions in superconducting quantum processors. We experimentally realize a transmon-C-shunt-transmon (TCT) device in which a flux-tunable, three-junction capacitively shunted flux-qubit coupler connects two transmon data qubits. The C-shunt coupler provides a flux-tunable, positively anharmonic spectrum for tailoring the interactions between the data qubits. Conditional Ramsey and swap measurements identify an idle region with near-zero residual ZZ interaction strength and suppressed transverse exchange. At this bias, simultaneous single-qubit interleaved randomized benchmarking yields X-gate fldelities above 99.7%, consistent with individual operation. A 45 ns nonadiabatic controlled-Z (CZ) gate achieves an interleaved randomized benchmarking fldelity estimate of 99.23(15)%. Numerical simulations identify coupler energy relaxation as an important limitation on CZ-gate fldelity and indicate that extending the coupler lifetime can improve gate performance. These results demonstrate the experimental feasibility of C-shunt flux-qubit couplers for combining low-interaction idling with fast entangling operations between transmon qubits.
